content.text: All preferred elements are present in §§ 22.1–22.2; no other audit right binds Customer.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: § 22.1 caps audits at once in any twelve-month period, requires thirty days' prior written notice, confines audits to normal business hours, and requires an off-site (where practicable) audit by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality. § 22.2 puts audit cost on Vendor unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent, and bars Vendor and its auditor from direct access to Customer systems (and from unrelated Customer Data, privileged material and third-party confidential information). This meets every element of our preferred position, not merely the fallback, and § 22.3 additionally treats findings as Customer Confidential Information. No other audit, inspection or verification right binding Customer exists in the document (§ 23 carries no operative text). No redline needed.
